model.name: Obligation / Commitment
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral structure for a directed deontic commitment: which party owes which action or forbearance, to whom, under which conditions, by when, to what standard, how it is discharged, and what follows if it is not.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-029 models a single obligation/commitment instance as a mixin that can be attached to any host record that creates or carries duties (contract clause, statute or regulation article, licence, court or administrative order, service commitment, internal policy, unilateral promise). It covers the deontic core (bearer, counterparty, modality, action), the conditional structure that detaches the duty, the temporal structure (due time, recurrence, grace, limitation), the lifecycle state model, fulfilment and its evidence, non-performance with excuse and remedy, the authority and provenance that make the duty defensible, and transfer, plurality and standards alignment. It deliberately does not model the instrument, the parties, the executed work or the accounting recognition; those are referenced from sibling models.
in_scope: Deontic modality of a single duty (obligation, prohibition, correlative right) and whether it is violable rather than definitional
Bearer/obligor, obligee, beneficiary, auxiliary and enforcing party roles for one commitment
Obligated action or forbearance, its controlled action term, refinements and subject matter or target
Antecedent and resolutive conditions, detachment, and the constraint expressions that gate the duty
Due instant or performance window, recurrence, grace, notice, survival and limitation periods
Lifecycle states and transitions with separate event time and observation/ingestion time
Fulfilment criteria, acceptance, discharge mode, partial performance and measure of progress
Fulfilment evidence, its issuer, integrity and status
Non-performance determination, excuse grounds, cure periods, remedy and penalty obligations
Legal or policy basis, issuing authority, jurisdiction and governing law of the duty
Record ownership, stewardship, provenance and audit trail of the obligation record
Assignment of the correlative right, transfer or novation of the duty, plurality of obligors/obligees and apportionment
Confidentiality classification, personal-data flags, retention and legal hold on obligation records
Crosswalk to ODRL Duty, LegalRuleML Obligation, FIBO contractual commitment, IFRS 15 performance obligation and compliance-obligation registers
out_of_scope: The agreement or contract instrument itself, its formation, offer/acceptance, consideration and clause text
Legal-entity identity, registration, legal capacity and party master data
Generic policy containers and rule engines, including access-control decision points and their evaluation infrastructure
Execution of work: tasks, work orders, scheduling, resourcing and dispatch
Payment initiation, clearing and settlement mechanics and ledger postings
Accounting recognition and measurement of liabilities, provisions and revenue amounts
Dispute, arbitration and litigation case management
Risk registers, control design and control-effectiveness testing
Consent capture and consent lifecycle as a lawful basis
Calendar, holiday and business-day-convention definitions themselves
Definitional or structural necessities that cannot be violated
Signature, sealing and e-signature ceremony records

boundary_notes.distinction: An agreement is a negotiated understanding reflecting offer and acceptance of commitments; a commitment is a promise by one party to act or refrain. One agreement carries many obligations, and an obligation can exist with no agreement at all (statute, court order, unilateral commitment, commitment at large). This model references the instrument and never restates its terms.

ODRL places Duties inside a Policy, either as a policy-level obligation or as a pre-condition duty on a Permission. This mixin sits at the Rule/Duty level, not the container level; the policy grouping, conflict strategy and inheritance belong to the policy model.

A right is the reciprocal aspect of a commitment and is borne by a different party; LegalRuleML models a Right as a permission to a bearer that implies obligations on auxiliary parties. The correlative right is referenced, not duplicated, so that assignment of the right and transfer of the duty stay separable.

A prohibition is violated by performing the act, an obligation by failing to perform it. The modality and violation polarity are recorded here, but negative-duty enforcement semantics (remedy on infringement) differ from consequence semantics on unfulfilled duties and must not be collapsed.

A task is an execution artefact. Several tasks may contribute to discharging one obligation, and tasks exist with no obligation behind them. Progress measurement is carried here only as a discharge measure, not as work scheduling.

IFRS 15 performance obligations are only promises to transfer distinct goods or services to a customer; obligations outside that definition fall to other standards. Recognition, measurement and presentation of the financial effect are out of scope and belong to a financial-reporting model.

ODRL defines Constraint as leftOperand/operator/rightOperand and LogicalConstraint as and/or/xone/andSequence. This model references those expression structures and their operand vocabularies rather than redefining operators.

A compliance management system maintains a register of obligations the organisation must or voluntarily chooses to meet. That register is a collection-level and programme-level concern; this model describes one obligation entry and does not carry control design or assurance results.

SBVR separates alethic necessities, which cannot be violated even in principle, from deontic obligations, which may be violated although they ought not to be. Structural necessities must not be represented as obligations in this model.

PROV-O supplies the entity/activity/agent vocabulary for how the obligation record came to be. This model aligns to it and carries the minimum provenance fields inline; the full provenance graph belongs to the provenance model.

bundles.name: Deontic Core and Parties
bundles.description: What kind of duty this is, who it identifies, who bears it and to whom it is owed. This is the irreducible core that every host record mixing in WM-XCT-029 must populate.
bundles.rationale: ODRL, LegalRuleML and FIBO independently converge on the same minimum: a deontic modality, an action, a bearer/obligor and (usually) a counterparty. Everything else in the model refines this core, so it is isolated as bundle one and kept free of instrument- and process-specific content.

layers.name: Identity, Versioning and Designation
layers.description: How one obligation is identified, versioned, and distinguished from the instrument that creates it and from the dated occurrences it generates.

findings.name: Obligation identity, versioning and occurrence distinction
findings.description: An obligation record needs a stable identity that survives amendment, is distinct from the clause or article that created it, and is distinct from each dated occurrence of a recurring duty. ODRL requires an IRI uid on a Policy and permits one on each Rule; LegalRuleML identifies statements so that associations, temporal characteristics and penalties can be attached to them. The identity rule must also state what makes two records the same obligation, because obligation data is typically extracted from documents by more than one process.

questions.text: Which system is the authoritative master for this obligation's identifier, and under which governed identifier scheme is it issued?
answer_data: Identifier scheme code or IRI namespace

questions.text: Does the identifier denote the standing obligation or one dated occurrence of a recurring duty?
When the obligation is amended, is the same identity versioned or is a superseding obligation created and linked?
What deterministic rule decides that two extracted records describe the same obligation?
answer_data: Match key definition (source citation + obligor + action + due basis)

data_elements.name: Obligation identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier for the obligation, assigned per the identity priority rule.

data_elements.name: Identifier scheme
data_elements.description: Governed scheme or IRI namespace under which the identifier was issued.

data_elements.name: Identity granularity
data_elements.description: Whether the record is the standing obligation or a single occurrence of it.

data_elements.name: Version label
data_elements.description: Version of the obligation record, distinct from the version of the source instrument.

data_elements.name: Supersedes reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the obligation record this one replaces on amendment or novation.

artifacts.name: Obligation register entry
artifacts.description: The durable, retrievable record of one obligation as held in the adopting Dimension's obligation register, carrying identity, core deontic fields and pointers to source and evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system identifier where an obligation master exists; otherwise a governed IRI minted in the Dimension's obligation namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID. The due date must never be used as the identifier.

layers.name: Deontic Modality and Obligation Typology
layers.description: The modal character of the duty and the classification axes that change how it is evaluated, measured and enforced.

findings.name: Deontic modality and violability
findings.description: The statement must be typed as an obligation, a prohibition, a permission or a right, because each has different violation conditions: LegalRuleML makes an obligation violated when the state or act is not achieved and a prohibition violated when it is achieved, and models a right as a permission to a bearer implying obligations on auxiliary parties. SBVR further separates deontic rules, which may be violated, from alethic necessities, which cannot; conflating them produces unenforceable or nonsensical obligation records.

questions.text: Which deontic modality does this statement carry, and which vocabulary term expresses it?
answer_data: Deontic modality code (obligation | prohibition | permission | right)

questions.text: Is the statement violable in principle, or is it a definitional necessity that cannot be breached?
Is violation triggered by omission of the action or by performance of it?
Which correlative right does this commitment create, and which party holds it?

data_elements.name: Deontic modality
data_elements.description: Obligation, prohibition, permission or right, expressed as a governed code.

data_elements.name: Violability class
data_elements.description: Whether the rule is deontic (violable) or alethic (definitional).

data_elements.name: Violation trigger polarity
data_elements.description: Whether violation follows from omission or from performance.

data_elements.name: Correlative right reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the reciprocal right created by this commitment.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Modality and violability are classification values evaluated with the obligation record itself and carried inline on it; the durable artefact is the obligation register entry and, where a contested classification is reviewed, the legal-basis citation record. Minting a separate modality artefact would fragment a single-valued field across two objects.

findings.name: Obligation typology: achievement, maintenance, result and effort
findings.description: Several orthogonal axes change evaluation. Achievement commitments are discharged by bringing about a condition, whereas maintenance commitments require a state to be kept true over an interval. UNIDROIT separates a duty to achieve a specific result from a duty of best efforts and gives criteria for determining which applies. Obligations are also primary or secondary (arising from breach of another), and only a subset of promises meet the IFRS 15 test of a distinct performance obligation.

questions.text: Is this an achievement obligation with a completion condition or a maintenance obligation over a state held across an interval?
answer_data: Completion condition or maintained state expression

questions.text: Is the obligor bound to achieve a specific result or only to exercise best efforts, and on what basis was that determined?
answer_data: Determination basis (express term, nature of obligation, risk allocation)

questions.text: Is this a primary obligation or a secondary obligation arising from breach of another?
Does this promise qualify as a distinct performance obligation for revenue-recognition purposes?
Is the obligation externally imposed or a commitment the organisation voluntarily set for itself?

data_elements.name: Obligation kind
data_elements.description: Achievement or maintenance character of the commitment.

data_elements.name: Effort standard
data_elements.description: Duty to achieve a specific result versus duty of best efforts.

data_elements.name: Primary or secondary obligation
data_elements.description: Whether the obligation is original or remedial.

data_elements.name: Performance obligation flag
data_elements.description: Whether the promise is a distinct performance obligation under IFRS 15.

data_elements.name: Compliance obligation category
data_elements.description: Externally imposed requirement or voluntary commitment, for register classification.

artifacts.name: Obligation classification scheme
artifacts.description: Versioned scheme defining the permitted values and decision criteria for obligation kind, effort standard, primary/secondary and compliance category, with the evidence trail for each criterion.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI per term in the Dimension's obligation-vocabulary namespace, with a version identifier on the scheme release.

layers.name: Bearer, Counterparty and Enforcement Roles
layers.description: The party structure of a directed commitment: who is bound, who is owed, who benefits, who may enforce or release.

findings.name: Obligor, capacity and delegated performance
findings.description: FIBO defines the obligor as the party bound legally or by agreement to do or refrain from doing something; LegalRuleML calls this the Bearer. ODRL adds a hard constraint that the party obligated to perform a duty must have the ability to exercise the duty action. Accountability must be separated from performance: delegating execution to an agent or subcontractor does not by itself move the duty.

questions.text: Which party bears the obligation, and under which authoritative party identifier is it recorded?
Does the bearer have the capability and legal capacity to exercise the obligated action?
Is performance delegated to another party, and does the bearer remain accountable for it?
Can one party hold both obligor and obligee roles for the same obligation, and what validation prevents that?

data_elements.name: Obligor reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party or parties bound by the obligation.

data_elements.name: Capacity and capability assertion
data_elements.description: Assertion that the bearer is able and legally competent to perform the obligated action.

data_elements.name: Performing party reference
data_elements.description: Party actually carrying out performance where it differs from the bearer.

data_elements.name: Accountability retained flag
data_elements.description: Whether the original bearer remains accountable despite delegated performance.

artifacts.name: Party role assignment record
artifacts.description: Record binding party references to obligor, performing-party and accountable-party roles for one obligation, with the effective period of each assignment.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Composite of the obligation identifier and the party identifier plus the role code and effective-from timestamp; no independent identifier is minted.

findings.name: Obligee, beneficiary and enforcement authority
findings.description: FIBO defines the obligee as the party to whom a commitment is owed and the beneficiary as the party that profits from it; the two can differ. FIBO also recognises a commitment at large made without direct involvement of the potential beneficiaries, which is why an identified obligee cannot be mandatory. ODRL expresses these roles as assigner and assignee function terms and allows a party collection refined by constraints. The right to enforce, waive or release must be recorded separately from the right to benefit.

questions.text: To whom is the obligation owed, and is that an identified party or a refined class of parties?
Is there a beneficiary distinct from the obligee, and what does the beneficiary receive?
Is this a directed commitment or a commitment at large with no identified beneficiary?
Which party is entitled to enforce, waive or release this obligation, and may it do so unilaterally?

data_elements.name: Obligee reference
data_elements.description: Party or party collection to whom the obligation is owed.

data_elements.name: Obligee collection refinement
data_elements.description: Constraint expression identifying the members of an obligee collection.

data_elements.name: Beneficiary reference
data_elements.description: Party receiving the benefit where distinct from the obligee.

data_elements.name: Directedness
data_elements.description: Whether the commitment is directed to identified parties or made at large.

data_elements.name: Enforcing party reference
data_elements.description: Party entitled to enforce, waive or release the obligation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Obligee, beneficiary and enforcing-party designations are reference data pointing into the sibling party model; the enforceable artefact that establishes them is the source instrument, already covered by the obligation source citation record. Creating a separate obligee artefact would duplicate party master data that this model explicitly excludes.

bundles.name: Obligated Content, Conditions and Standards
bundles.description: What must actually be done, on what subject matter, under what conditions, to what standard and in what quantity.
bundles.rationale: ODRL makes the Action mandatory on every Rule and gates duties through Constraints; UNIDROIT supplies the substantive determinants of content (implied terms, quality, place, currency, partial performance); IFRS 15 supplies the measure-of-progress machinery. These are grouped because they jointly answer 'what counts as doing it', which is the precondition for any fulfilment test.

layers.name: Obligated Action and Subject Matter
layers.description: The controlled action or forbearance and the asset, sum, information or place it operates on.

findings.name: Obligated action term, refinement and forbearance
findings.description: ODRL requires exactly one Action on every Rule, requires every action term other than use and transfer to declare an includedIn parent reaching use or transfer transitively, and allows refinements that narrow the action, with a caution that refinement should not reduce the action to a null operation. LegalRuleML admits a state, an act or a course of action as the object of a deontic specification, which is what allows forbearances and standing conduct rules to be expressed.

questions.text: What exactly must be done or forborne, expressed as a single controlled action term?
answer_data: Natural-language statement of the obligated behaviour

questions.text: Which action vocabulary governs the term, and to which broader action does it roll up?
What refinements narrow the action, and has the refined action been checked against becoming a null operation?
Is the obligated behaviour a single act, a course of action, or the maintenance of a state?

data_elements.name: Action term
data_elements.description: Governed term naming the obligated action or forbearance.

data_elements.name: Action vocabulary reference
data_elements.description: Profile or vocabulary that defines the action term and its hierarchy.

data_elements.name: Action refinement
data_elements.description: Constraints narrowing the semantics of the action.

data_elements.name: Action narrative
data_elements.description: Verbatim or paraphrased statement of the obligated behaviour from the source instrument.

data_elements.name: Forbearance flag
data_elements.description: Whether the duty is to refrain rather than to act.

artifacts.name: Statement of obligated action
artifacts.description: The extracted clause, article or specification text that states what must be done, held alongside its controlled-term encoding so that the encoding remains auditable against the wording.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed citation identifier of the source instrument plus the clause or article locator; the extract carries no independent identity.

findings.name: Target subject matter, place and currency of performance
findings.description: ODRL binds rules to a target Asset, optionally an AssetCollection refined by constraints, and warns that refinement should not yield an empty set. UNIDROIT supplies the default place of performance, the payment rules and the currency rules where the parties are silent. Many statutory duties have no asset at all, so the target must be optional on a duty even though ODRL requires exactly one target on permissions and prohibitions.

questions.text: What asset, resource, information item or sum of money is the target of this obligation?
answer_data: Assertion that the obligation is target-free where none applies

questions.text: Where must performance occur or be delivered, and is that place stated or defaulted?
If the obligation is monetary, in what currency and by what mechanism must it be discharged?
If the target is a collection, what refinement identifies its members and has the resulting set been checked as non-empty?

data_elements.name: Target reference
data_elements.description: Asset, resource or item the obligated action applies to.

data_elements.name: Target collection refinement
data_elements.description: Constraint expression selecting the members of a target collection.

data_elements.name: Place of performance
data_elements.description: Location at which performance must occur or be delivered.

data_elements.name: Monetary amount
data_elements.description: Amount owed where the obligation is monetary.

data_elements.name: Currency
data_elements.description: Currency in which a monetary obligation must be discharged.

artifacts.name: Performance and delivery schedule
artifacts.description: Schedule identifying, per obligation or occurrence, the target items, the place and mode of delivery, and any monetary amounts and currencies.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Obligation identifier plus schedule line number; the schedule as a whole takes the identifier of the instrument annex it belongs to.

layers.name: Conditions, Detachment and Constraint Expression
layers.description: The conditional structure that makes a duty become due, lapse or never arise, and the formal expressions used to state it.

findings.name: Antecedent condition, detachment and interference
findings.description: Most commitments are conditional: the duty exists but only becomes due when its antecedent holds. UNIDROIT distinguishes a suspensive condition, which delays effect, from a resolutive condition, which terminates it, imposes a duty to preserve the other party's rights while the condition is pending, and makes improper interference with the occurrence of a condition actionable. ODRL expresses the equivalent gate as constraints that must all be satisfied. Detachment is an observable event and must be timestamped and attributable.

questions.text: What antecedent must hold before the obligation becomes due, and is the condition suspensive or resolutive?
answer_data: Effect on the obligation when satisfied

questions.text: What observable event or data proves the antecedent is satisfied, and which party asserts it?
What follows if a party improperly prevents or brings about the occurrence of the condition?
Is the obligation unconditional, that is, is its antecedent constantly true?
What must each party do while the condition is still pending?
answer_data: Restitution rule on failure of the condition

data_elements.name: Antecedent expression
data_elements.description: Formal expression of the condition that detaches the obligation.

data_elements.name: Condition type
data_elements.description: Suspensive or resolutive character of the condition.

data_elements.name: Detachment time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the antecedent became satisfied.

data_elements.name: Detachment evidence reference
data_elements.description: Evidence supporting the assertion that the antecedent was satisfied.

data_elements.name: Interference finding
data_elements.description: Recorded determination that a party interfered with the occurrence of the condition.

artifacts.name: Condition evaluation log
artifacts.description: Append-only log of each evaluation of an obligation's antecedent and constraints, recording the operand values observed, the outcome, the evaluator and both the event time and the observation time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Obligation identifier plus a monotonically increasing evaluation sequence number; each entry additionally carries the evaluating agent reference.

findings.name: Constraint and logical-constraint expression form
findings.description: ODRL defines a Constraint as exactly one leftOperand, exactly one operator and either a rightOperand or a rightOperandReference, optionally with unit and dataType, and defines LogicalConstraint over existing constraints with the operands and, or, xone and andSequence, requiring order preservation for andSequence. Multiple constraints on the same rule are a conjunction. An obligation model that stores conditions as free text loses all of this and cannot be evaluated.

questions.text: How is each condition expressed as left operand, operator and right operand, with unit and datatype where needed?
How are multiple constraints combined: conjunction, disjunction, exclusive-one or ordered sequence?
answer_data: Ordered member list where sequence matters

questions.text: Which operand and operator vocabulary is authoritative, and what must a processor do with terms it does not recognise?
How is an unsatisfiable or self-contradictory constraint set detected before the obligation is activated?

data_elements.name: Left operand
data_elements.description: Governed term naming the quantity or attribute being constrained.

data_elements.name: Operator
data_elements.description: Relational or set operator applied between operands.

data_elements.name: Right operand
data_elements.description: Literal, IRI, term or list compared against the left operand, or a reference resolving to one.

data_elements.name: Constraint unit
data_elements.description: Unit of measure qualifying the operand values.

data_elements.name: Logical operand kind
data_elements.description: and, or, xone or andSequence combination over member constraints.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Constraint expressions are inline structured expressions of the obligation record, evaluated in place; ODRL itself models them as nested nodes of a rule rather than as separately identified resources, and their durable output is already captured by the condition evaluation log. Materialising each constraint as an artefact would create identity for nodes the source standard leaves unidentified.

layers.name: Performance Standard and Quantification
layers.description: The quality bar the performance must meet and the quantity or progress by which discharge is measured.

findings.name: Quality of performance and conformity assessment
findings.description: Where an instrument does not fix quality, UNIDROIT requires performance of a quality that is reasonable and not less than average in the circumstances, so an obligation record must state whether the standard is express or defaulted. Practical obligations add thresholds, tolerances and a named conformity assessor. Note that this finding has only partial primary support: the service-level-objective structure normally used here derives from cloud SLA standards that could not be retrieved, so thresholds are modelled generically.

questions.text: What quality or service standard must the performance meet, and is that standard express or defaulted?
What threshold or tolerance separates conforming from non-conforming performance?
Who determines conformity, and by what test or method?
When the referenced standard changes mid-life, does the new version apply to open occurrences?

data_elements.name: Performance standard reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the quality or service standard the performance must meet.

data_elements.name: Standard source
data_elements.description: Whether the standard is expressly agreed, implied by law or defaulted to reasonableness.

data_elements.name: Threshold value
data_elements.description: Numeric threshold or tolerance defining conformity.

data_elements.name: Conformity assessor reference
data_elements.description: Party competent to determine whether performance conforms.

data_elements.name: Measurement method
data_elements.description: Test, sampling or calculation method used to assess conformity.

artifacts.name: Acceptance criteria and service level schedule
artifacts.description: Schedule stating, per obligation, the quality standard, thresholds, measurement method, measurement window and the party competent to assess conformity.
media_or_form: annex or schedule to an instrument
artifacts.identity_strategy: Instrument annex identifier plus obligation identifier; individual criteria are addressed by criterion code within the schedule.

findings.name: Quantity owed, partial performance and measure of progress
findings.description: Discharge is often quantitative. UNIDROIT lets the obligee refuse a partial tender at the due time unless it has no legitimate interest in refusing, while IFRS 15 measures progress toward complete satisfaction of an obligation satisfied over time. ODRL supplies count and payAmount operands for quantity-based constraints. Outstanding balance must be derivable at any instant, which requires the fulfilled quantity to be recorded as an accumulation rather than a flag.

questions.text: What quantity, amount or count fully discharges this obligation?
Is partial performance permitted at the due time, and does it proportionally reduce the outstanding amount?
By what method is progress toward complete satisfaction measured?
answer_data: Progress method code (input or output based)
Progress percentage at the measurement instant

questions.text: What is the outstanding quantity at a given instant, and how is it recomputed after each contribution?

data_elements.name: Obligation quantity
data_elements.description: Total quantity or amount required for complete discharge.

data_elements.name: Fulfilled quantity
data_elements.description: Cumulative quantity performed and accepted to date.

data_elements.name: Outstanding quantity
data_elements.description: Remaining quantity required, derived from obligation and fulfilled quantities.

data_elements.name: Progress measurement method
data_elements.description: Method used to measure progress toward complete satisfaction.

data_elements.name: Partial performance allowed
data_elements.description: Whether a partial tender may be refused at the due time.

artifacts.name: Progress measurement record
artifacts.description: Dated record of measured progress or delivered quantity against one obligation, with the method applied, the inputs used and the resulting outstanding balance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Obligation identifier plus measurement sequence number and measurement instant; where an external meter is the source, its reading identifier is retained as a cross-reference.

bundles.name: Temporal Structure and Lifecycle
bundles.description: When the duty bites, how often, for how long it remains enforceable, and the states it passes through.
bundles.rationale: LegalRuleML attaches temporal characteristics with legal status and status development to norms; UNIDROIT fixes time of performance and limitation; RFC 3339 fixes the representation. Time and state are grouped because state transitions are timestamped events and every state predicate in this model is time-indexed.

layers.name: Due Time, Recurrence and Enforceability Window
layers.description: The instant or window for performance, its repetition, the tolerances around it, and the outer bound of enforceability.

findings.name: Due instant, performance window and time basis
findings.description: UNIDROIT distinguishes a fixed time, a period within which the obligor may choose the moment, and performance within a reasonable time where nothing is fixed; that distinction changes when non-performance can be declared and must be a first-class field, not implied by the presence or absence of a due date. RFC 3339 requires seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and gives -00:00 a distinct meaning when the local offset is unknown. Legal deadlines stated in local civil time must retain their timezone and business-day basis, since an early conversion to a UTC instant destroys the legal meaning.

questions.text: What is the due instant or performance window, expressed with seconds and an explicit offset or Z?
Is the time fixed, a period within which the obligor may choose, or an unspecified reasonable time?
Which time zone, calendar and business-day convention adjusts the nominal due date?
Where the deadline runs from a trigger event, what is the offset rule and from which event instant does it run?
answer_data: Computed due timestamp and computation time

data_elements.name: Due time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant by which performance must occur.

data_elements.name: Performance window
data_elements.description: Start and end bounds of the period within which performance may be rendered.

data_elements.name: Due basis
data_elements.description: Fixed time, obligor-chosen period, reasonable time or event-derived.

data_elements.name: Time zone reference
data_elements.description: Time zone or civil-time locale in which the deadline is legally expressed.

data_elements.name: Business-day convention
data_elements.description: Rule adjusting a nominal due date that falls on a non-business day.

data_elements.name: Derived due rule
data_elements.description: Offset rule computing the due time from a trigger event.

artifacts.name: Due date schedule
artifacts.description: Per-obligation schedule of nominal and adjusted due instants with their basis, time zone and business-day treatment, produced so that deadline computation is reproducible and reviewable.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Obligation identifier plus occurrence key; schedule releases carry a version identifier and a generation timestamp.

findings.name: Recurrence, grace periods and notice requirements
findings.description: Many commitments repeat on a rule rather than existing as one dated duty, so occurrences must be generated deterministically and remain individually addressable. Grace periods delay the declaration of non-performance without moving the due time. Notice duties are themselves obligations, often with their own lead times and recipients, and ODRL provides an inform action and informed-party function for exactly this shape. Amending a recurrence rule mid-life must not silently rewrite settled history.

questions.text: Does the obligation recur, and by what deterministic rule are its occurrences generated?
What grace period runs after the due time before non-performance may be declared?
What notice must be given, to whom, and how far in advance, before the obligation bites or is enforced?
When the recurrence rule is amended, how are already generated and already settled occurrences treated?

data_elements.name: Recurrence rule
data_elements.description: Deterministic expression generating occurrences of a repeating obligation.

data_elements.name: Occurrence key
data_elements.description: Key identifying one generated occurrence of a recurring obligation.

data_elements.name: Grace duration
data_elements.description: Period after the due time before non-performance may be declared.

data_elements.name: Notice lead duration
data_elements.description: Advance period by which required notice must precede the event it concerns.

data_elements.name: Notice recipient reference
data_elements.description: Party or parties entitled to receive required notice.

artifacts.name: Occurrence and notice schedule
artifacts.description: Generated list of obligation occurrences with their due instants, grace expiry and the notices required before each, retained so that occurrence generation can be replayed and audited.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Obligation identifier plus occurrence sequence number; the generating rule version and generation timestamp are recorded on every generated row.

findings.name: Limitation periods, survival and enforceability
findings.description: An obligation can be substantively owed yet no longer enforceable. UNIDROIT devotes a chapter to limitation periods, and LegalRuleML models temporal characteristics as pairs of time with a legal status and a status development, letting efficacy, applicability and enforceability be tracked separately. Survival after termination of the instrument is a distinct question from limitation. Both drive retention, since GDPR permits continued retention where necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims.

questions.text: For how long after the due time does the obligation remain legally enforceable, and under which law is that period fixed?
Does the obligation survive termination or expiry of the instrument that created it?
Which events suspend, interrupt or restart the limitation period?
How does the enforceability window justify continued retention of the obligation and its evidence?

data_elements.name: Limitation period
data_elements.description: Period after which the obligation ceases to be enforceable.

data_elements.name: Limitation start basis
data_elements.description: Event from which the limitation period runs.

data_elements.name: Survival flag
data_elements.description: Whether the obligation continues after the instrument ends.

data_elements.name: Enforceability end
data_elements.description: Instant after which enforcement is time-barred.

data_elements.name: Tolling event reference
data_elements.description: Event suspending or restarting the limitation period.

artifacts.name: Limitation and survival determination
artifacts.description: Reviewed determination recording the governing law, the applicable limitation period, any tolling events and whether the obligation survives termination, used as the retention justification for the obligation record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Obligation identifier plus determination date and determining party; superseded determinations are retained and linked rather than overwritten.

layers.name: Lifecycle State Model
layers.description: The permitted states of an obligation, the transitions between them and the timestamps that make the history reconstructible.

findings.name: Obligation states, transitions and dual timestamps
findings.description: An obligation moves through states that must be explicit rather than inferred: proposed, active but conditional, detached and due, in performance, partly fulfilled, fulfilled or discharged, breached, excused, waived or released, cancelled, transferred, expired and superseded. ODRL derives fulfilment from constraint satisfaction plus exercise of the refined action, and treats a duty as unfulfilled unless its consequences are also fulfilled; LegalRuleML makes Violation and Compliance explicit indications. Every transition needs both the instant the change legally took effect and the instant the system observed or ingested it, because these routinely differ for externally evidenced events. Maintenance commitments additionally need transient breach distinguished from terminal breach.

questions.text: Which states may this obligation occupy, and which transitions between them are permitted?
Is state derived by evaluating conditions and evidence, or asserted by an authorised party?
answer_data: Deriving rule or asserting party reference

questions.text: How are the event time and the observation or ingestion time of each state change recorded separately?
May an obligation return to an open state after being marked fulfilled, and on whose authority?
For a maintenance obligation, how is a transient lapse distinguished from a terminal breach?

data_elements.name: Current state
data_elements.description: Governed state code the obligation currently occupies.

data_elements.name: State entered at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the state change legally took effect.

data_elements.name: State observed at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the state change was observed or ingested by the recording system.

data_elements.name: State basis
data_elements.description: Whether the state was derived by evaluation or asserted by a party.

data_elements.name: Transition history
data_elements.description: Ordered collection of prior state transitions with their timestamps, actors and reasons.

data_elements.name: Terminal state flag
data_elements.description: Whether the current state closes the obligation to further transitions.

artifacts.name: Obligation state transition log
artifacts.description: Append-only log of every state change of an obligation, capturing prior and new state, event time, observation time, the acting agent, the triggering evidence and the rule or authority relied on.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Obligation identifier plus a gapless, monotonically increasing transition sequence number; entries are never updated or deleted, only superseded by later entries.

bundles.name: Fulfilment and Non-Performance
bundles.description: What discharges the duty and what happens when it is not discharged.
bundles.rationale: ODRL gives an operational fulfilment test and a consequence mechanism, LegalRuleML gives Violation, Compliance, PenaltyStatement and Reparation, and UNIDROIT gives the substantive law of non-performance, force majeure and hardship. Together they define the two outcomes an operating agent must be able to compute and defend.

layers.name: Fulfilment, Acceptance and Evidence
layers.description: The test for complete discharge, the role of obligee acceptance, and the evidence that proves performance.

findings.name: Fulfilment criteria, acceptance and discharge mode
findings.description: ODRL states that a duty is fulfilled if all its constraints are satisfied and its action, with all refinements satisfied, has been exercised, and that where the action has not been exercised all consequences must be fulfilled instead. IFRS 15 ties satisfaction to transfer of control, either over time or at a point in time. Acceptance by the obligee is a separate step from performance and must not be conflated with it; discharge can also occur by substitute performance, set-off, waiver or release, each of which is a different discharge mode with different evidential needs.

questions.text: What conjunction of conditions constitutes complete fulfilment of this obligation?
Does discharge require obligee acceptance, and within what period may acceptance be withheld?
By which mode was the obligation discharged: performance, substitute performance, set-off, waiver, release or expiry?
When does control or benefit transfer, and does that instant determine discharge?

data_elements.name: Fulfilment criteria
data_elements.description: Expression of the conditions that together constitute complete discharge.

data_elements.name: Acceptance required
data_elements.description: Whether obligee acceptance is a precondition of discharge.

data_elements.name: Accepted at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the obligee accepted performance.

data_elements.name: Discharge mode
data_elements.description: Manner in which the obligation ceased to be owed.

data_elements.name: Discharged at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the obligation was fully discharged.

artifacts.name: Acceptance or completion certificate
artifacts.description: Issued record by which the obligee or a competent assessor accepts performance and confirms discharge, including the criteria assessed and any reservations.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuer-assigned certificate number within a governed series, cross-referenced to the obligation identifier and, where applicable, the occurrence key.

findings.name: Fulfilment evidence, integrity and revocation
findings.description: An obligation record without evidence is an assertion, not a defensible fact. The Verifiable Credentials Data Model supplies the shape for competent, tamper-evident evidence: an issuer, a validity interval, a credential status for revocation or suspension, a proof and an explicit evidence property describing how the issuer verified the claims. PROV-O supplies attribution and the generating activity. Evidence must bind to the specific occurrence and quantity it discharges, and later revocation or correction must be able to reopen a settled state.

questions.text: What evidence is required to demonstrate performance, and who is competent to issue it?
How are the integrity and authenticity of fulfilment evidence verified?
How is each evidence item bound to the specific occurrence and quantity it discharges?
What happens when evidence is later revoked, corrected or found insufficient?

data_elements.name: Evidence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an item of evidence supporting performance.

data_elements.name: Evidence type
data_elements.description: Kind of evidence, such as receipt, attestation, telemetry or credential.

data_elements.name: Evidence issuer reference
data_elements.description: Party that issued and vouches for the evidence.

data_elements.name: Evidence integrity proof
data_elements.description: Cryptographic proof or signature establishing authenticity and integrity.

data_elements.name: Evidence status
data_elements.description: Current validity of the evidence, including revocation or suspension.

artifacts.name: Fulfilment evidence package
artifacts.description: Bounded set of evidence items supporting discharge of one obligation or occurrence, retained with issuer, validity interval, integrity proof and status so that discharge can be re-verified after the fact.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuer-assigned credential or document identifier where one exists; otherwise a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID for the package, always cross-referenced to the obligation identifier.

layers.name: Non-Performance, Excuse and Remedy
layers.description: Determining and declaring breach, the grounds that excuse it, and the secondary obligations it produces.

findings.name: Non-performance determination and declaration
findings.description: UNIDROIT treats non-performance as failure to perform any obligation, expressly including defective performance and late performance, so a model that records only a missed deadline is incomplete. LegalRuleML marks Violation as an explicit indication attached to a deontic specification, and Compliance as its counterpart. Who may declare breach, whether formal notice is required, whether the breach is fundamental, and how a contested determination is held pending resolution are all separate decisions that must be recorded rather than derived.

questions.text: What form does non-performance take here: non-delivery, defective performance, or lateness?
answer_data: Reference to the criterion not met

questions.text: Who determines and declares breach, and is formal notice a precondition to remedies?
Is the breach material or fundamental, and what threshold decides that?
How is a disputed breach determination represented while it remains unresolved?

data_elements.name: Breach type
data_elements.description: Form of non-performance: non-delivery, defective, late or other.

data_elements.name: Breach declared at
data_elements.description: Instant at which non-performance was formally declared.

data_elements.name: Declaring party reference
data_elements.description: Party that determined and declared the non-performance.

data_elements.name: Materiality assessment
data_elements.description: Recorded assessment of whether the breach is material or fundamental.

data_elements.name: Dispute status
data_elements.description: Whether the breach determination is accepted, contested or under review.

artifacts.name: Breach or default notice
artifacts.description: Formal notice served on the non-performing party stating the obligation, the failure, the evidence relied on and any cure period, retained with proof of service.
media_or_form: structured notice record with delivery proof
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuer notice number within a governed series, cross-referenced to the obligation identifier and carrying an RFC 3339 service timestamp with explicit offset.

findings.name: Excuse grounds, cure periods and consequence obligations
findings.description: UNIDROIT excuses non-performance for an impediment beyond the party's control under force majeure and provides a separate hardship regime for events fundamentally altering the equilibrium of performance. ODRL models the repercussions of not fulfilling a duty through the consequence property and the repercussions of infringing a prohibition through remedy, and expressly forbids a consequence duty from itself carrying a further consequence. LegalRuleML links a PenaltyStatement to a prescriptive statement through Reparation. Consequence and remedy duties are themselves obligations, so this model recurses onto itself.

questions.text: What grounds excuse non-performance, and what notice and proof does an excuse require?
answer_data: Effect on the obligation (suspended, extinguished, renegotiated)

questions.text: Is there a cure period during which late performance still discharges the original obligation?
answer_data: Effect of cure on accrued remedies

questions.text: Which consequence or remedy obligations are triggered by non-fulfilment, and are they registered as obligations in their own right?
answer_data: Creation timestamp of the secondary obligation

questions.text: What formula, cap or ceiling limits penalties and damages?
May a consequence obligation itself carry a further consequence, and how is that reconciled with the exchange format's prohibition on nesting?
answer_data: Recorded divergence from the exchange format

data_elements.name: Excuse ground
data_elements.description: Recorded ground excusing non-performance, such as force majeure or hardship.

data_elements.name: Cure period
data_elements.description: Period during which performance still discharges the original obligation.

data_elements.name: Remedy obligation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a consequence or remedy obligation created by non-fulfilment.

data_elements.name: Penalty formula
data_elements.description: Rule computing damages, interest or penalty amounts.

data_elements.name: Penalty cap amount
data_elements.description: Contractual or statutory ceiling on the amount payable.

artifacts.name: Remedy and penalty determination record
artifacts.description: Record of the remedies and penalties determined to apply following non-performance, the excuse grounds considered and rejected or accepted, the amounts computed and the secondary obligations created.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Determination number within a governed series, linked to both the breached obligation identifier and the identifiers of any secondary obligations created.

bundles.name: Authority, Provenance and Record Governance
bundles.description: What makes the obligation legitimate and defensible, who stewards the record, and how it is protected, audited and retained.
bundles.rationale: LegalRuleML makes Authority and Jurisdiction first-class, PROV-O supplies the record-provenance vocabulary, GDPR imposes concrete constraints on retaining obligation records containing personal data, and ISO 37301 frames the obligation register as a maintained management-system artefact. Without this bundle an obligation record cannot be relied on in a dispute.

layers.name: Legal Basis, Authority and Jurisdiction
layers.description: The instrument and authority that create the duty and the legal space in which it operates.

findings.name: Source instrument, citation precision and issuing authority
findings.description: Obligations arise from contracts, statutes and regulations, licences, court and administrative orders, internal policies and unilateral commitments. FIBO models the contractual commitment as a provision of a contract, so a contractual obligation must cite its clause, not merely its instrument. LegalRuleML defines an Authority as a person or organisation with power to create, endorse or enforce legal norms. ISO 37301 treats obligations as spanning externally imposed requirements and commitments the organisation adopts voluntarily, which changes who may amend or withdraw them.

questions.text: Which instrument creates this obligation, and at what clause or article-level citation?
Which authority issued or endorsed the norm, and does it have power to enforce it?
answer_data: Power to create, endorse or enforce

questions.text: Is the obligation externally imposed or a commitment the organisation set for itself?
How is an amendment to the source instrument propagated to obligation records derived from it?

data_elements.name: Source instrument reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the contract, statute, order, licence or policy creating the obligation.

data_elements.name: Source citation
data_elements.description: Clause, article or paragraph-level locator within the source instrument.

data_elements.name: Source kind
data_elements.description: Category of the creating instrument.

data_elements.name: Issuing authority reference
data_elements.description: Authority that created, endorsed or enforces the norm.

data_elements.name: Source version
data_elements.description: Version or consolidated-text date of the source instrument relied on.

artifacts.name: Obligation source citation record
artifacts.description: Record binding an obligation to the exact instrument version and clause locator it derives from, with the extraction method and reviewer, so that the derivation can be re-checked against the authoritative text.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Obligation identifier plus source instrument identifier, instrument version and clause locator; the citation record has no independent identity.

findings.name: Jurisdiction, governing law and applicability window
findings.description: LegalRuleML defines Jurisdiction as a geographic area or subject matter over which an Authority applies its legal power, and models temporal characteristics with a legal status and status development, which is how efficacy, applicability and enforceability windows are kept distinct. The same factual duty can be governed by different law for different parties, and conflicting mandatory rules across jurisdictions must be recorded as a conflict rather than silently resolved.

questions.text: Which jurisdiction's law governs the obligation, and which forum resolves disputes about it?
Over what territory or subject matter does the issuing authority's power extend?
Where two jurisdictions impose conflicting duties, which prevails and how is the conflict recorded?
During which period was the governing norm in force, applicable to this party, and enforceable?

data_elements.name: Governing law reference
data_elements.description: Legal system governing the obligation.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction
data_elements.description: Territorial or subject-matter jurisdiction of the issuing authority.

data_elements.name: Dispute forum reference
data_elements.description: Court, tribunal or arbitral body competent to resolve disputes.

data_elements.name: Applicability period
data_elements.description: Interval during which the norm applies to this bearer, distinct from its in-force period.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction conflict note
data_elements.description: Recorded conflict between duties imposed by different jurisdictions.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Governing law, jurisdiction and forum are reference values resolving into the legal-instrument and jurisdiction registries maintained by sibling models; the authoritative artefact is the choice-of-law clause in the source instrument, already addressed by the obligation source citation record. Minting a jurisdiction artefact here would create a competing copy of registry data this model excludes.

layers.name: Stewardship, Accountability and Provenance
layers.description: Who is answerable for the obligation record and how its history is proved.

findings.name: Record ownership, monitoring duty and review cadence
findings.description: A compliance management system keeps its obligations current and accessible to those who need them, which implies a named owner, a monitoring responsibility, a review cadence and an escalation route. These are distinct from the obligor: the party that owes the duty is often not the party that maintains the record about it. PROV-O's actedOnBehalfOf and qualified Delegation give the vocabulary for recording that separation without losing the chain of responsibility.

questions.text: Who owns this obligation record and is accountable for its accuracy and completeness?
Who monitors performance against this obligation and raises alerts before the due time?
How often is the record reviewed for currency, and who attests that it is current?
What is the escalation path when the responsible party is absent, unresponsive or conflicted?

data_elements.name: Record owner reference
data_elements.description: Party accountable for the accuracy of the obligation record.

data_elements.name: Monitoring party reference
data_elements.description: Party responsible for monitoring performance and raising alerts.

data_elements.name: Review cadence
data_elements.description: Interval at which the record must be reviewed for currency.

data_elements.name: Last reviewed at
data_elements.description: Instant of the most recent currency review.

data_elements.name: Escalation path
data_elements.description: Ordered escalation route when the responsible party cannot act.

artifacts.name: Obligation ownership and review record
artifacts.description: Record of the accountable owner, monitoring assignment, review cadence and each completed currency review of an obligation register entry.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Obligation identifier plus owner reference and effective-from timestamp; each review adds a dated entry rather than replacing the prior one.

findings.name: Record provenance, derivation and tamper-evident audit trail
findings.description: PROV-O supplies the minimum: which Agent the record is attributed to, which Activity generated it, which Entity it was derived from, and when that activity started and ended. For obligations extracted from documents by automated processes, the derivation link to the source clause is what makes the record contestable and correctable. Assertion time, event time and ingestion time must be kept apart, and the audit trail must be append-only if it is to be relied on after a dispute begins.

questions.text: Which agent and activity generated this obligation record, using which inputs, and when?
How is a derived obligation traced back to the clause or rule it was extracted from, and with what confidence?
answer_data: Confidence score and human review status

questions.text: How are assertion time, event time and ingestion time distinguished throughout the audit trail?
answer_data: Offset or Z designator on each

questions.text: Is the audit trail append-only and tamper-evident, and how is that demonstrated to a third party?

data_elements.name: Generating activity reference
data_elements.description: Activity that produced or last modified the obligation record.

data_elements.name: Attributed agent reference
data_elements.description: Agent to whom the obligation record is attributed.

data_elements.name: Derived-from reference
data_elements.description: Source entity, such as a clause or prior record, from which this record was derived.

data_elements.name: Record created at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the obligation record was created.

data_elements.name: Record ingested at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the record entered this system, distinct from creation and event time.

data_elements.name: Integrity digest
data_elements.description: Digest or proof establishing that the record has not been altered since recording.

artifacts.name: Provenance and change audit trail
artifacts.description: Append-only trail of every creation, amendment, derivation and access decision affecting an obligation record, with agent, activity, inputs, reasons and separated event, assertion and ingestion timestamps.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Obligation identifier plus a gapless audit sequence number; each entry carries an integrity digest chaining it to its predecessor.

layers.name: Confidentiality, Access and Retention
layers.description: Classification, lawful basis, retention and deletion of obligation records and their evidence.

findings.name: Confidentiality classification, personal data and retention
findings.description: Obligation records routinely name individuals, so they attract data-protection constraints: storage limited to what is necessary, an identified lawful basis where processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation, and erasure rights that yield where retention is necessary for a legal obligation or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims. Retention must therefore be justified by the enforceability window rather than set arbitrarily, and destruction must distinguish full deletion from tombstoning that preserves referential integrity.

questions.text: What confidentiality classification applies, and who may read, amend, close or export the obligation?
Does the record or its evidence contain personal data, and on what lawful basis is it processed?
How long are the obligation record and its evidence retained after discharge, and on what justification?
How do erasure requests interact with legal holds and defence-of-claims retention?
At end of retention, what is destroyed and what is tombstoned to preserve referential integrity?

data_elements.name: Confidentiality classification
data_elements.description: Classification governing who may access the obligation record.

data_elements.name: Personal data flag
data_elements.description: Whether the record or its evidence contains personal data.

data_elements.name: Lawful basis
data_elements.description: Basis relied on for processing personal data in the record.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Period for which the record is retained after its retention trigger.

data_elements.name: Retention trigger
data_elements.description: Event from which the retention period runs, such as discharge or end of enforceability.

data_elements.name: Legal hold flag
data_elements.description: Whether destruction is suspended because of an actual or anticipated claim.

artifacts.name: Retention and access schedule
artifacts.description: Schedule stating, per obligation class, the confidentiality classification, permitted operations by role, retention trigger and period, legal hold rules and the end-of-retention destruction or tombstoning treatment.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Schedule identifier with a version and effective-from timestamp; individual rules are addressed by rule code within the version.

bundles.name: Structure, Transfer and Interoperability
bundles.description: How obligations relate to each other, how they move between parties, and how they map to external standards.
bundles.rationale: UNIDROIT devotes whole chapters to assignment, transfer and plurality, and prescribes the order and interdependence of performances; ODRL and LegalRuleML define the exchange forms this model must map to without overclaiming conformance. These concerns are separated because they operate on the obligation as a whole rather than on its content.

layers.name: Composition and Dependency
layers.description: Parent-child decomposition and interdependence between obligations.

findings.name: Decomposition, order of performance and reciprocal dependency
findings.description: UNIDROIT fixes the order of performance where obligations are interdependent, and IFRS 15 asks whether a promise is distinct or so integrated with others that it cannot stand alone; both are decomposition questions with operational consequences. A parent obligation discharged only when all children are discharged behaves differently from an obligation merely grouped with others for reporting. Reciprocal dependency, where each party's duty is conditional on the counterparty's, is a common source of deadlock and must be represented explicitly, along with a check against circular dependency.

questions.text: Is this obligation decomposed into sub-obligations, and does discharging all children discharge the parent?
What ordering or interdependency exists between this obligation and the counterparty's obligations?
Is the obligation distinct and separable, or so integrated with others that it cannot be performed alone?
How are circular or self-referential dependencies detected and prevented before activation?

data_elements.name: Parent obligation reference
data_elements.description: Obligation of which this one is a constituent part.

data_elements.name: Child obligation reference
data_elements.description: Constituent sub-obligations of this obligation.

data_elements.name: Dependency type
data_elements.description: Nature of dependency on another obligation, such as prerequisite, reciprocal or concurrent.

data_elements.name: Performance order
data_elements.description: Required sequence relative to interdependent obligations.

data_elements.name: Distinctness assessment
data_elements.description: Recorded assessment of whether the promise is distinct or integrated.

artifacts.name: Obligation dependency map
artifacts.description: Graph of parent-child and dependency relations among obligations arising from one instrument or programme, with the cycle-detection result and the derived performance sequence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Instrument or programme identifier plus map version and generation timestamp; edges are keyed by the pair of obligation identifiers and the dependency type.

layers.name: Transfer, Substitution and Plurality
layers.description: Movement of the duty or its correlative right between parties, and multi-party structures on either side.

findings.name: Assignment of rights, transfer of duties and novation
findings.description: UNIDROIT treats assignment of rights and transfer of obligations as separate regimes, alongside assignment of contracts as a whole; a right can usually be assigned more freely than a duty can be transferred, and transferring a duty raises whether the original obligor is released or remains bound. This directly determines identity continuity: a release-and-substitute novation is best modelled as a new obligation superseding the old, whereas a delegation of performance leaves identity intact. FIBO's commitment at large explains why some commitments are transferable as instruments in their own right.

questions.text: May the correlative right be assigned, and does the obligor's consent or notice condition the assignment?
May the duty be transferred, and is the original obligor released or retained as guarantor?
On transfer or novation, does the obligation keep its identifier or does a successor obligation take over?
What instrument evidences the transfer, and from which instant is it effective against each party?

data_elements.name: Transferability flag
data_elements.description: Whether the right or duty may be transferred.

data_elements.name: Transfer type
data_elements.description: Assignment of right, transfer of duty, delegation of performance or novation.

data_elements.name: Transfer effective at
data_elements.description: Instant from which the transfer takes effect.

data_elements.name: Original obligor released
data_elements.description: Whether the original obligor is discharged by the transfer.

data_elements.name: Successor obligation reference
data_elements.description: Obligation record that continues the duty after a novation.

artifacts.name: Assignment or novation record
artifacts.description: Instrument-backed record of a transfer of a right or duty, naming the transferor, transferee, consenting parties, effective instant, release status and the identity continuity decision applied.
media_or_form: notice of assignment with proof of service
artifacts.identity_strategy: Transfer instrument identifier where one exists, otherwise a governed series number, always linked to the predecessor and successor obligation identifiers.

findings.name: Plurality of obligors and obligees, and apportionment
findings.description: UNIDROIT devotes a chapter to plurality of obligors and obligees, which is where joint and several liability, divided shares, contribution between co-obligors and solidary obligees are settled. A model that stores a single obligor reference cannot express a syndicate, a consortium, a group of guarantors or a class of claimants, and cannot compute who may be pursued for how much. Apportionment must also carry a default rule for the common case where the instrument is silent.

questions.text: Where several parties are bound, is liability joint and several or divided into shares?
How are shares apportioned, and what is the default when the instrument is silent?
May the obligee demand full performance from any one obligor, and what contribution follows between co-obligors?
Where several obligees exist, may any of them demand full performance and give a valid discharge?

data_elements.name: Liability mode
data_elements.description: Joint, several, joint and several, or divided liability among obligors.

data_elements.name: Share allocation
data_elements.description: Per-party allocation of the obligation among co-obligors or co-obligees.

data_elements.name: Default share rule
data_elements.description: Rule applied to apportion shares where the instrument is silent.

data_elements.name: Obligee solidarity mode
data_elements.description: Whether any single obligee may demand full performance and validly discharge the obligation.

data_elements.name: Contribution claim reference
data_elements.description: Claim by a performing co-obligor against the others for their shares.

artifacts.name: Liability apportionment schedule
artifacts.description: Schedule recording co-obligors and co-obligees, the liability mode, each party's share, the default rule applied where the instrument is silent, and contribution entitlements after performance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Obligation identifier plus party identifier and effective-from timestamp for each share row; the schedule version is recorded on every row.

layers.name: Standards Alignment and Exchange
layers.description: Mapping to external obligation vocabularies, with recorded conflicts and honest conformance claims.

findings.name: Crosswalk to external obligation vocabularies and recorded conflicts
findings.description: This model must exchange with ODRL Duty, LegalRuleML Obligation and PenaltyStatement, FIBO contractual commitment, IFRS 15 performance obligation and compliance-obligation registers, but the mappings are not clean. ODRL binds permissions and prohibitions to exactly one target Asset, which does not fit duties with no asset; ODRL forbids a consequence duty from carrying its own consequence, whereas escalation chains in law are open-ended; ODRL requires a processor to stop when it does not recognise a profile identifier; and the IFRS 15 sense of obligation is far narrower than the legal sense. Each divergence must be recorded as a conflict, not resolved silently, and conformance must never be claimed without evidence of validation.

questions.text: To which external term does each element map, and is the mapping exact, broader, narrower or merely related?
Which constraints of the target vocabulary does the mapping violate, such as required targets or consequence nesting limits?
Which conflict-resolution strategy applies when a permission and a prohibition on the same action collide?
What is asserted as formal conformance rather than mere alignment, and what validation evidence supports it?
Which profile identifiers must a consuming processor recognise, and what must it do when it does not?

data_elements.name: Alignment target term
data_elements.description: External vocabulary term to which a model element is mapped.

data_elements.name: Mapping relation
data_elements.description: Exact, broader, narrower or related character of the mapping.

data_elements.name: Conformance claim
data_elements.description: Scope of any formal conformance asserted, or an explicit statement that only alignment is claimed.

data_elements.name: Validation report reference
data_elements.description: Evidence produced by a validator supporting a conformance claim.

data_elements.name: Known conflict
data_elements.description: Recorded divergence between this model and a target vocabulary.

artifacts.name: Alignment crosswalk table
artifacts.description: Versioned table mapping each element of this model to terms in ODRL, LegalRuleML, FIBO, IFRS 15 and compliance-obligation registers, with the mapping relation, the supporting citation and the recorded conflicts.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Crosswalk identifier with a version and the pinned versions of every target vocabulary; each row is keyed by source element identifier plus target term IRI.

functions.name: Register obligation
functions.description: Create an obligation record from a source instrument clause, statutory article, order or voluntary commitment, populating the deontic core and the source citation.
inputs: Source instrument reference and clause locator
Obligor and, where directed, obligee references
outputs: Obligation register entry with an assigned identifier
Provenance entry for the creating activity
preconditions: The source instrument version is resolvable and its clause locator is valid
The action term resolves in a declared action vocabulary
The obligor reference resolves in the party model
effects: A new obligation identity exists in the register
The obligation enters the proposed or active state with both event and ingestion timestamps recorded

functions.name: Classify obligation
functions.description: Assign modality, violability, achievement or maintenance kind, effort standard, primary or secondary status and compliance category, with the criteria applied.
preconditions: The classification scheme version is published and effective
The obligated action is stated
effects: Downstream evaluation and measurement rules are selected by the assigned classes
Alethic statements are rejected from the obligation register

functions.name: Evaluate antecedent and detach
functions.description: Evaluate the obligation's antecedent and constraint set against observed operand values and, when satisfied, detach the obligation so that it becomes due.
inputs: Observed operand values with their observation times
preconditions: All left operands resolve in a recognised profile
The evaluator recognises every declared profile identifier
effects: The obligation transitions to detached or remains conditional
A durable, replayable evaluation record is appended

functions.name: Compute due schedule
functions.description: Derive due instants and performance windows from the due basis, recurrence rule, time zone, business-day convention and any trigger events.
inputs: Time zone, calendar and business-day convention
outputs: Due date schedule with nominal and adjusted instants
preconditions: The calendar and business-day convention references resolve
Every input instant carries an explicit offset or Z
effects: Occurrences become individually addressable and monitorable
Deadline computation becomes reproducible from recorded inputs

functions.name: Evaluate fulfilment
functions.description: Determine whether the obligation is fulfilled by testing constraint satisfaction and exercise of the refined action, accounting for quantity, acceptance and any consequence duties.
preconditions: Evidence supporting exercise of the action is present and unrevoked
Acceptance has been given or is not required
effects: The obligation transitions toward fulfilled, partly fulfilled or unchanged
Outstanding balances are recomputed

functions.name: Record fulfilment evidence
functions.description: Attach evidence of performance to an obligation or occurrence with its issuer, validity interval, integrity proof and status, and bind it to the quantity it discharges.
preconditions: The issuer is recognised as competent for this evidence type
The integrity proof verifies against the evidence
effects: Discharge becomes independently re-verifiable
Later revocation of the evidence can reopen the determination

functions.name: Declare non-performance
functions.description: Determine and formally declare non-performance after the due time and grace period, classify it, assess materiality and serve any required notice.
inputs: Evidence of failure, defect or lateness
outputs: Breach or default notice with proof of service
preconditions: The grace period has expired without discharge
No accepted excuse ground is in force
The declaring party is authorised
effects: Consequence and remedy obligations become eligible for creation
The dispute status field becomes available for contestation

functions.name: Apply remedy or penalty
functions.description: Create the consequence, remedy or penalty obligations triggered by non-fulfilment or infringement, compute amounts against the formula and cap, and link them to the breached obligation.
inputs: Penalty formula, cap and accrual basis
outputs: Links from the breached obligation to its consequences
preconditions: Breach has been declared and any cure period has expired
The consequence definition does not itself carry a further consequence in the exchange projection
effects: Secondary obligations enter the register with their own lifecycles
The original obligation remains open until both it and its consequences are fulfilled

functions.name: Transfer obligation or assign right
functions.description: Record assignment of the correlative right, transfer of the duty, delegation of performance or novation, applying the identity continuity rule and any release of the original obligor.
preconditions: The right or duty is transferable under the governing instrument
Any required consent or notice has been obtained and evidenced
effects: Party roles change from the effective instant
Identity is preserved for delegation and replaced for release-and-substitute novation

functions.name: Transition obligation state
functions.description: Apply a permitted state transition, recording the prior and new state, the basis, the acting agent, the event time and the observation time.
