inputs: Current state and proposed target state
outputs: Updated current state and terminal flag
preconditions: The transition is permitted by the declared transition matrix
The acting agent holds the required authority for asserted transitions
effects: The obligation history remains reconstructible at any past instant
Terminal states block further transitions except authorised reopening

functions.name: Report obligation register
functions.description: Produce a filtered, access-controlled view of obligations by owner, state, due window, jurisdiction or source, for monitoring, management review and assurance.
preconditions: The requester holds read access at the requested scope
Confidentiality classifications are resolved for every selected row
effects: Register currency and coverage become measurable
Every disclosure is auditable

functions.name: Apply retention and close
functions.description: Evaluate the retention trigger, enforceability window and legal holds, then archive, tombstone or destroy the obligation record and its evidence, certifying the outcome.
preconditions: No legal hold is in force
Retention justification has been reviewed against the limitation determination
effects: Records are removed or reduced to tombstones while referential integrity is preserved
Data-protection storage limitation is demonstrably observed

composition.target: Host record carrying duties (contract clause, statute or regulation article, licence condition, service commitment, internal policy statement, unilateral pledge)
composition.purpose: WM-XCT-029 is applied to any host record that creates or carries a duty, supplying the deontic core, conditions, due structure, lifecycle and fulfilment semantics without changing the host's own identity or content model.
Resolve the instrument, its version and the clause locator that creates a contractual obligation; the instrument's formation, consideration and clause text stay in that model.
Resolve obligor, obligee, beneficiary, performing, enforcing and monitoring party references, including legal capacity, without duplicating party master data.
Link the correlative right created by the commitment so that assignment of the right and transfer of the duty remain separately governed.
Compose the antecedent, refinement and rule constraints from a shared expression structure of left operand, operator, right operand, unit and logical combination.

composition.target: Obligation / Commitment (WM-XCT-029) as consequence, remedy or penalty obligation
composition.purpose: Secondary obligations created by non-fulfilment or infringement are themselves obligations and recurse onto this model rather than being modelled as flat penalty attributes.
Resolve fulfilment evidence, notices, certificates and their issuers, validity intervals, proofs and revocation status.

Align obligation-record provenance to Entity, Activity and Agent with generation, derivation, attribution, association and delegation, so that derived obligations remain traceable to their source clause.
Provide a machine-evaluable exchange projection for duties, actions, constraints, consequences and remedies, with recorded divergences on asset targeting and consequence nesting.

composition.target: OASIS LegalRuleML 1.0 Obligation, Violation and PenaltyStatement
composition.purpose: Provide a legal-norm exchange projection carrying bearer, auxiliary party, violation, compliance, reparation, authority, jurisdiction and temporal characteristics.
Flag the narrower accounting subset of promises and their satisfaction pattern, without importing recognition or measurement into this model.
Supply the per-entry structure that a compliance obligations register aggregates, covering both externally imposed requirements and voluntary commitments.
Resolve retention triggers, periods, legal holds and destruction treatment for obligation records and their evidence.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension MUST designate one accountable owner package for WM-XCT-029 and record it in the Dimension registry before any obligation record is created; unowned obligation records MUST be rejected at creation.

The owner package MUST publish and version the controlled vocabularies this model depends on — deontic modality, violability class, obligation kind, effort standard, discharge mode, state set and transition matrix, breach type, excuse ground and transfer type — as resolvable terms with effective dates.

The owner package MUST declare which host models may mix in this model and which sibling models are referenced rather than duplicated, and MUST re-declare that list whenever a sibling model changes its scope.

The owner package MUST nominate a legal or compliance reviewer accountable for jurisdiction-bearing fields (governing law, limitation, survival, enforcement authority) and MUST NOT allow those fields to be set by automated extraction without review.
The owner package MUST maintain the alignment crosswalk with pinned versions of every target vocabulary and MUST record divergences rather than silently adapting them.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint obligation identifiers and vocabulary terms in a single stable namespace controlled by the owner package, segmented by concern (obligations, occurrences, states, actions, excuse grounds). Never reuse an external standard's namespace for locally defined terms; where a local term corresponds to an external one, record the correspondence in the crosswalk with an explicit mapping relation. Term IRIs are opaque and permanent: retire terms by deprecation with a replacement pointer, never by reuse or deletion. Occurrence keys are minted under the parent obligation's namespace so that they remain resolvable after the parent is superseded.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-xct-029 (WM-XCT-029, entry kind mixin, nav path NAV.XCT.OBL, domain tag XCT.OBL) is the authoritative registration for this model and MUST carry the owner package and review state.
The registry entry MUST link to the sibling models named in the composition section once their registry identifiers exist, replacing the descriptive target names used here.

The registry entry MUST record the review state boundary-review-required until the boundaries against the agreement, right, policy and compliance-register models have been signed off by the nominated reviewer.

canonicalization_rules: All timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; the originally stated local time, its time zone identifier and its business-day convention are retained alongside the canonical instant and are never discarded.
Code values are canonicalised to their governed term IRIs; display labels are derived, never stored as the authoritative value.
Quantities are canonicalised as an explicit value-plus-unit pair, and monetary amounts as an explicit amount-plus-currency pair; bare numbers are rejected.
Absent and empty are distinguished: an omitted element means not asserted, an explicit null means asserted as not applicable, and an empty collection means asserted as none.
References are canonicalised to resolvable identifiers with the referenced version pinned where the referent is versioned, so that a citation continues to mean what it meant when recorded.
patch_rules: Patches address stable element identifiers, never positional paths, so that reordering a collection never changes the meaning of a stored patch.
State changes are appended as transitions and never applied as in-place overwrites of the current state; the current state is a derived projection of the transition log.

Changes to deontic modality, obligor, obligated action, due basis or governing law create a new version with a supersedes link rather than mutating the existing record, because these fields change what the obligation is.
Every patch carries the acting agent, the reason code, the event time and the ingestion time; a patch missing any of these is rejected.
Corrections to historical facts are recorded as corrective entries that preserve the superseded value, so that what the register said at any past instant remains reconstructible.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional element, a new vocabulary term or a new alignment mapping is a minor change.

Adding a required element, narrowing a cardinality, removing an element, or removing or redefining a state, modality or discharge-mode code is a breaking change and requires a major version and a migration note.
Changing the transition matrix to forbid a previously permitted transition is breaking; adding a permitted transition is minor only if no terminal state gains an outbound transition.

Retargeting the crosswalk to a new version of an external vocabulary is minor when the conformance claim is unchanged, and breaking when a previously asserted conformance claim is withdrawn or narrowed.
Consumers MUST tolerate unknown optional elements, and MUST stop processing rather than guess when they encounter an unrecognised profile identifier.

identity_priority: Use the identifier assigned by the authoritative master system for the obligation where such a master exists, for example the obligation identifier issued by a contract-management or regulatory-register system of record.
Otherwise use a governed global identifier or IRI minted in the owner package's obligation namespace, resolvable and permanent.
Otherwise mint a UUID or ULID under the adopting Dimension's control and record the minting agent and instant.
A due date, a clause number, a party name or any combination of descriptive attributes is never an identifier; such combinations may serve only as declared match keys for deduplication.
Occurrence identity is always composite: the standing obligation identifier plus the occurrence key generated by the recorded recurrence rule version.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Every timestamp is an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Event time (when the fact took legal effect) and observation or ingestion time (when the system learned of it) are recorded as separate elements and are never collapsed; where a legally relevant local civil time exists, its time zone identifier and business-day convention are stored alongside the canonical instant. The RFC 3339 -00:00 form is used only to mean that the local offset is genuinely unknown and is never written as a synonym for Z.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts — state transition log entries, condition evaluation entries, progress measurements, acceptance certificates, breach notices, remedy determinations, assignment records and audit entries — are numbered within a series scoped to one obligation identifier, using a gapless monotonically increasing integer with no semantic content. The series name encodes the artefact class and the obligation identifier; gaps are treated as evidence of loss and must be investigated, and numbers are never reissued after voiding.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Append-only artefacts (state transition log, condition evaluation log, provenance and change audit trail) carry a per-entry integrity digest chained to the preceding entry, so that removal or alteration of any entry is detectable. Externally issued evidence retains its issuer's proof and status endpoint unaltered; the register stores the verification outcome and instant rather than re-signing the evidence. Any artefact whose integrity check fails is quarantined, flagged on the obligation record and excluded from fulfilment evaluation until resolved.

policies: An obligation record MUST NOT be created without a resolvable source instrument reference and a clause, article or paragraph-level citation; obligations asserted without a stated basis are held as candidates and excluded from the operative register.
Alethic statements MUST NOT be registered as obligations; a statement that cannot in principle be violated belongs to the definitional vocabulary, not to the obligation register.

Conformance to an external standard MUST NOT be claimed without a dated validation report from a named validator; absent that evidence, only alignment may be asserted and the divergences must be listed.

Automated extraction MAY populate an obligation record, but jurisdiction-bearing fields and any transition into breached, waived, released or discharged states MUST be attributable to an authorised human or explicitly delegated agent.

Deleting an obligation record is prohibited while it is within its enforceability window or under legal hold; disposal outside those constraints proceeds through the retention function and produces a destruction or tombstone record.

Fulfilment MUST NOT be asserted on the basis of elapsed time alone; discharge requires the recorded fulfilment test to be satisfied or an explicit discharge mode such as waiver, release, set-off or expiry to be recorded with its instrument.

read: Reading an obligation returns its current state as a projection of the transition log together with the event and ingestion timestamps of the latest transition.

Reads are filtered by confidentiality classification and requester role; suppressed elements are reported as suppressed rather than silently omitted, so that consumers cannot mistake redaction for absence.
Historical reads at a past instant MUST be supported and MUST return what the register asserted at that instant, not the current values.
create: Creation requires identifier assignment under the identity priority, a source citation, a deontic modality, an obligated action and an obligor; records failing any of these are rejected, not stored as partial.
Creation records the generating activity, the attributed agent and both creation and ingestion timestamps.
Creating a recurring obligation also records the recurrence rule version used, so that generated occurrences can be replayed.
update: Content-defining fields (modality, obligor, action, due basis, governing law) are updated only by versioning with a supersedes link; other fields are patched in place with a reason code and dual timestamps.
State is never updated directly; it changes only through the recorded transition function against the declared transition matrix.
Updates to a superseded version are prohibited; corrections apply to the current version and cite the superseded one.
delete: Hard deletion is prohibited for obligations within their enforceability window, under legal hold, or referenced by an open secondary obligation.
End-of-retention disposal reduces the record to a tombstone retaining the identifier, the disposal decision and the destruction certificate reference, so that inbound references do not dangle.
Append-only logs are never deleted individually; they are disposed only as whole series under a recorded retention decision, and the disposal is itself logged.

roles.name: Obligation Model Owner
responsibilities: Own the specification, vocabularies and version history of WM-XCT-029 within the adopting Dimension
Approve breaking changes, migrations and the declared list of host and sibling models
Maintain the registry entry and drive the outstanding boundary review to closure

roles.name: Obligation Registrar / Steward
responsibilities: Create and maintain obligation records, assign identifiers under the identity priority and keep source citations accurate
Run currency reviews at the declared cadence and attest that register entries remain correct
Resolve duplicate and merge decisions against the declared match key

roles.name: Legal and Compliance Reviewer
responsibilities: Review and approve modality, violability, governing law, jurisdiction, limitation and survival determinations
Approve breach declarations, excuse determinations and waiver or release decisions
Record conflicts between jurisdictions or between this model and external vocabularies rather than resolving them silently

roles.name: Performance Monitor
responsibilities: Track due schedules, grace expiry and progress measurements and raise alerts within the declared lead times
Attach fulfilment evidence and record verification outcomes
Escalate impending or actual non-performance along the recorded escalation path

roles.name: Records and Retention Officer
responsibilities: Apply retention triggers, legal holds and disposition to obligation records and their evidence
Issue destruction certificates and maintain tombstone integrity
Reconcile erasure requests against enforceability-window and legal-claim retention justifications

roles.name: Interoperability Custodian
responsibilities: Maintain the alignment crosswalk with pinned target-vocabulary versions and recorded divergences
Run validators against exchange projections and retain dated validation reports
Block conformance claims that lack validation evidence

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Access is granted per scope to named roles, and every grant carries a purpose and an expiry; obligation records are readable only by roles with a declared need arising from ownership, monitoring, legal review, assurance or a party's own involvement.
exceptions: The obligor and obligee of an obligation may read the findings and artefacts describing their own duty, its due structure, its fulfilment state and the evidence relied on against them, even where the general classification is more restrictive.
Auditors, supervisory authorities and courts may be granted time-boxed read access across all scopes for a stated proceeding, recorded as an exception with its legal basis, scope and expiry.
Legal hold suspends any access restriction that would prevent preservation, but does not by itself widen read access.

Automated evaluators may read constraint expressions, operand values and state at finding scope without access to free-text clause extracts or personal data, so that evaluation does not require broad disclosure.
audit_requirements: Every read, export and access-exception grant is logged with the requester, role, scope, purpose, decision and RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset.
Every state transition, version supersession and patch is logged with acting agent, reason code, event time and ingestion time in the append-only audit trail.
Access to obligation records containing personal data is separately reportable so that disclosure can be reconstructed for a data-subject or supervisory request.
Audit trails are retained for at least the enforceability window of the obligation they concern and are disposed of only under a recorded retention decision.

read_order: AGENTS.md — establish Name, Type, owner package, registry identifier and the four required URLs before touching any record
Specification URL — read the model scope, boundaries, bundle/layer/finding structure and the required elements, so that records are interpreted with the correct semantics
Storage type URL — learn the concrete projection in use (document store, graph, files under version control, or a service) and the canonicalisation and patch rules that apply to it
Interface URL — learn the available operations, their authorisation scopes and the required timestamp and identifier formats
Processes URL — learn the registration, classification, evaluation, breach, remedy, transfer and retention procedures and the roles authorised to run them
Vocabulary namespace and alignment crosswalk — resolve controlled terms and check pinned external vocabulary versions before producing any exchange projection

coverage.claim: This structure covers the deontic core, party roles, obligated content, conditional detachment, temporal and lifecycle behaviour, fulfilment and its evidence, non-performance with excuse and remedy, legal basis and jurisdiction, record stewardship and provenance, confidentiality and retention, composition, transfer, plurality and standards alignment for a single directed obligation used as a mixin. It is grounded in W3C ODRL 2.2 (duty, action, constraint, consequence, remedy, fulfilment test), OASIS LegalRuleML 1.0 (deontic specification, bearer, violation, compliance, penalty, reparation, authority, jurisdiction, temporal characteristics), EDM Council FIBO (contractual commitment, obligor, obligee, commitment at large), UNIDROIT Principles 2016 (implied terms, result versus best efforts, conditions, time/place/currency of performance, non-performance, force majeure, hardship, assignment and transfer, limitation, plurality), IFRS 15 (performance obligation, satisfaction over time or at a point in time, measure of progress), IETF RFC 3339 (timestamps), W3C PROV-O (provenance), W3C VC 2.0 (evidence), OMG SBVR (deontic versus alethic) and EU Regulation 2016/679 (retention and erasure). Service-level-objective structure and the operational requirements of an obligations register are gaps with only partial primary support.

checklist.notes: Identity priority, scheme, standing-versus-occurrence granularity, versioning by supersession and an explicit deduplication match key; explicitly excludes dates and descriptive attribute combinations as identifiers. Grounded in ODRL uid requirements, LegalRuleML statement identification and FIBO commitment structure.

Explicit state set, transition matrix, derived-versus-asserted state basis, terminal states, authorised reopening and transient-versus-terminal breach for maintenance obligations. Grounded in the ODRL fulfilment test, LegalRuleML Violation/Compliance and the achievement/maintenance distinction from AAAI 2021.

Obligor, obligee, beneficiary, auxiliary and enforcing roles; correlative right link; parent-child decomposition; ordering and reciprocal dependency; plurality with joint and several liability and contribution. Grounded in FIBO party roles, LegalRuleML bearer/auxiliary party and UNIDROIT Chapters 6 and 11.

Due basis distinguishing fixed time, obligor-chosen period, reasonable time and event-derived deadlines; recurrence, grace, notice lead times, limitation, survival and enforceability windows; all instants RFC 3339 with explicit offset and separated event and observation times.

Generating activity, attributed agent, derived-from links to the source clause, extraction method and confidence, creation and ingestion timestamps, and a chained tamper-evident audit trail. Aligned to PROV-O starting-point and qualified terms.

Record owner separated from obligor; monitoring assignment, review cadence, attestation and escalation path; delegated performance with retained accountability expressed through PROV-O delegation. Register-upkeep grounding from ISO 37301 is scope-level only.

Constraint consistency and unsatisfiability checks, non-empty collection refinement checks, null-operation checks on action refinement, role disjointness, cycle detection on dependencies, and conformance claims gated on dated validator evidence. Grounded in the ODRL Validator and Evaluator roles.

Deny-by-default with scoped grants across bundle, layer, finding and artifact; party self-access, supervisory and judicial exceptions, and a narrowed evaluator scope that excludes free text and personal data. Every read and grant is logged.

Retention triggered by discharge or end of enforceability and justified by the limitation determination; legal hold; erasure reconciled against the legal-obligation and legal-claims exceptions; hard deletion prohibited in-window with tombstoning to preserve referential integrity. Grounded in GDPR Articles 5(1)(e), 6(1)(c), 17 and 30 and UNIDROIT Chapter 10.

Crosswalk with mapping relations, pinned target versions, recorded divergences, conflict-resolution strategy, profile identification and the requirement to halt on unrecognised profiles; conformance separated from alignment.
Obligation, prohibition, permission and right typed explicitly, with violation polarity and the SBVR deontic-versus-alethic filter that keeps definitional necessities out of the register.
Suspensive and resolutive conditions, detachment timestamps and evidence, duties pending the condition, interference findings, and ODRL constraint and logical-constraint expression form.

Fulfilment test as constraint satisfaction plus exercise of the refined action, acceptance as a separate step, discharge modes, and evidence with issuer, validity interval, integrity proof and revocation status aligned to VC 2.0.

Non-performance covering non-delivery, defect and lateness; declaration authority and notice; materiality; excuse grounds; cure periods; and consequence, remedy and penalty obligations that recurse onto this model.
Quantity owed, partial performance, cumulative fulfilled and outstanding quantities, and input- or output-based measure of progress from IFRS 15, with penalty formulae and caps.

Thresholds, tolerances and measurement windows are modelled generically because the cloud SLA standard normally relied on (ISO/IEC 19086-1) returned HTTP 403 and could not be read. Only UNIDROIT 5.1.6 reasonable-quality grounding is primary; treat the SLO shape as unsupported structure pending retrieval.

Register upkeep, currency and accessibility requirements rest on the ISO 37301 committee scope statement only; the normative clause text is paywalled and was not read, so review cadence, escalation and register completeness requirements are presented as practice, not as cited normative requirements.
Place of performance with stated-versus-default indicator, jurisdictional territory and subject-matter extent, and ODRL spatial operands. Grounded in UNIDROIT 6.1.6 and LegalRuleML Jurisdiction.

Place of performance is a reference into a location or party model rather than a geometry; no coordinate reference system, precision or topology requirement arises from the sources for a general obligation mixin.

Integrity digests chained across append-only logs, quarantine of artefacts failing integrity checks, verification of external proofs without re-signing, and authority requirements for state assertions.
Personal data flag, lawful basis, minimised evaluator access, and separately reportable access to personal data. Grounded in GDPR Articles 6(1)(c) and 30.

Assignment of rights, transfer of duties, delegation of performance and novation, each with consent or notice requirements, release status and an explicit identity continuity rule. Grounded in UNIDROIT Chapter 9.

known_omissions: ISO/IEC 19086-1 (cloud SLA framework, service level objectives and service qualitative objectives) could not be retrieved; the standard's page returned HTTP 403. The performance-standard finding therefore lacks the primary grounding that would normally define threshold, metric and measurement-window structure.
The normative text of ISO 37301:2021 is paywalled; only the ISO/TC 309 committee scope statement was read. Obligations-register requirements are therefore treated as gap-level support.

Multiagent commitment-protocol literature that formalises the operations create, cancel, release, delegate and assign over C(debtor, creditor, antecedent, consequent) could not be machine-read (the AAMAS commitment-alignment PDF failed to parse). The state model is grounded in ODRL, LegalRuleML and UNIDROIT, with the achievement-versus-maintenance distinction taken from the AAAI 2021 abstract only; the finer-grained commitment operations are deliberately not asserted.

The OMG SBVR specification page yielded title, version and date but not the clause text on deontic and alethic modality; the distinction as used here is supported at the level of SBVR's stated purpose plus secondary commentary, so the violability filter is a weaker claim than the ODRL and LegalRuleML groundings.
Insolvency effects on obligations — automatic stay, set-off on insolvency, subordination and rescission of preferences — are not modelled and would materially change enforceability.
Tax, prudential and sector-specific statutory obligation catalogues are not enumerated; only GDPR is used as a worked statutory example.

Non-Western and non-commercial obligation frameworks (Shariah-compliant structures, customary and community obligations, family-law duties) are not addressed; the model's grounding is commercial and regulatory.

Distributed-ledger or self-executing settlement semantics are treated as an interface projection and are not modelled; automated execution introduces determinism and finality questions this model does not answer.
Negotiation and pre-contractual commitments (letters of intent, memoranda of understanding, comfort letters) are not distinguished from binding commitments beyond the violability filter.
Aggregate and portfolio-level views — exposure across obligations, netting, and covenant baskets — are out of scope; this model describes one obligation at a time.
conflicts: ODRL requires exactly one target Asset on a Permission and a Prohibition, and models actions as operations on assets. Many legal and regulatory obligations (file a return, maintain insurance, appoint an officer) have no asset. ODRL's Duty allows zero-or-one target, so duties remain expressible, but any projection that routes obligations through permissions will misfit; recorded as a divergence rather than resolved.

ODRL forbids a consequence Duty from itself carrying a consequence, and forbids a remedy from referring to a Duty that includes a consequence. Legal escalation chains are open-ended (interest on unpaid damages, penalties on unpaid penalties). This model recurses onto itself for secondary obligations and therefore cannot round-trip deep escalation chains through ODRL without flattening; the flattening strategy must be recorded.

LegalRuleML models a Right as a Permission to a bearer implying obligations on auxiliary parties, while FIBO models a Commitment as a promise giving rise to both an obligation and a reciprocal right. The modelling unit differs — a normative statement versus a promise — so a one-to-one mapping between LegalRuleML Right and FIBO Commitment must not be assumed.

The IFRS 15 sense of performance obligation is narrower than the legal sense: it covers only promises to transfer distinct goods or services to a customer, and obligations falling outside it are addressed by other standards. Treating the accounting flag as a general obligation classifier would misclassify most regulatory and internal obligations.

ODRL distinguishes a policy-level obligation from a duty attached as a pre-condition of a permission, with different fulfilment consequences. Collapsing both into a single obligation field loses the distinction between a freestanding duty and a duty that gates an entitlement.

RFC 3339 requires an explicit offset, but many legal deadlines are stated in local civil time with a business-day convention and no offset. Canonicalising to a UTC instant at capture destroys legally relevant information; this model retains both representations, which means the canonical instant alone is not authoritative for deadline disputes.

ODRL requires a processing system to stop when it does not recognise a profile identifier, whereas obligation registers commonly need best-effort ingestion of partially understood external policies. Silent partial processing would breach the ODRL requirement; the model therefore requires an explicit halt-and-quarantine rather than lenient parsing.
regional_assumptions: The UNIDROIT Principles are soft law: they apply where the parties choose them, where they supplement an international instrument, or as gap-fillers. Their rules on best efforts, conditions, place and currency of performance, force majeure, hardship, assignment, limitation and plurality are used here as a well-attested reference frame, not as universally binding law.

Limitation periods, survival rules and the enforceability of penalty and liquidated-damages clauses vary materially by jurisdiction; several common-law systems restrict penalty clauses that civil-law systems permit. Specific durations and enforceability outcomes must be determined per governing law and are deliberately not asserted here.

GDPR-derived retention, erasure and lawful-basis structure applies to personal data within EU and EEA scope. Other regimes impose different retention floors and erasure rights, so the retention finding's mechanics are portable but its specific bases are not.

IFRS 15 applies where IFRS Accounting Standards are used; converged but non-identical national standards exist elsewhere, and jurisdictions on local GAAP may define performance obligations differently or not at all.

Business-day conventions, public holidays and civil-time offsets are jurisdiction-specific and are referenced from a calendar model rather than defined here; deadline computation is only as correct as that reference.

Notice service rules, including what counts as effective service and when it takes effect, are jurisdiction-specific; the model records service evidence and instants but does not assert validity of service.
adversarial_checks: Counterexample — commitment with no identified beneficiary. FIBO recognises a commitment at large made without direct involvement of potential beneficiaries. The model therefore makes the obligee reference optional (0..n) and adds an explicit directedness code, rather than requiring a counterparty as most contract-centric designs do.

Counterexample — negative obligation. A duty to refrain is violated by performing the act, not by omitting it. A single boolean 'fulfilled' flag would be meaningless here, so violation polarity is a required element and forbearance is flagged on the action, keeping prohibition semantics from being silently coerced into obligation semantics.

Counterexample — obligation with no asset. Statutory duties such as appointing a data protection officer or responding within one month have no target asset. Target references are therefore 0..n with an explicit assertion available for the target-free case, and the ODRL asset-targeting divergence is recorded rather than papered over.

Counterexample — maintenance obligation. A duty to keep insurance in force is not discharged by a single act and cannot be modelled by a due date plus a completion flag. The achievement/maintenance axis is a required classification and the state model requires transient lapse to be distinguishable from terminal breach.

Counterexample — obligation that is owed but unenforceable. Limitation and survival are modelled separately from discharge, so an obligation can be substantively outstanding while time-barred, which a simple open/closed state model cannot express.

Rejected structure — a priority, urgency or workload layer. Attractive for operations, but these are attributes of the work item that discharges the obligation, not of the duty itself; admitting them would duplicate the task model and make obligation records vary with staffing.

Rejected structure — a smart-contract or automation-execution layer. Self-execution is a property of a projection and an interface, not of the obligation's semantics; including it would violate the format-neutrality requirement and embed finality assumptions the sources do not support.

Rejected structure — an accounting recognition and provisioning layer. IFRS 15's boundary makes clear that recognition and measurement are a separate discipline; the model carries only the performance-obligation flag and the distinctness assessment, and refers the rest out.

Conflation test — obligation versus requirement or control. A compliance requirement in a register and an instantiated duty on a named bearer are different objects with different lifecycles; the model describes one entry and explicitly excludes control design and assurance results, keeping the register aggregation in a sibling model.

Overreach test — conformance claims. Every alignment is stated as a mapping with a relation and recorded conflicts, and the service layer forbids asserting conformance without a dated validation report, so no node in this structure claims standard conformance on the strength of resemblance alone.

Support test — every layer traced to primary sources. Two dimensions failed this test and are marked as gaps rather than presented as canonical: service-level objective structure (ISO/IEC 19086-1 unreachable) and obligations-register operations (ISO 37301 clause text paywalled).
